text:
mia: Quick check — I'd like to propose a very small "connector handshake" for SDK transports so clients and servers can negotiate prefetch/bundle capabilities without baking in a bunch of heuristics.
mia: Idea: transport advertises capability string in initial metadata; SDK surface picks one of: `no-prefetch`, `server-cursor`, `prefetch-window=N`, `bundle=small|large`. Also advertise `resume-token=true|false` and `dedupe-seq=true|false`.
mia: Example header we could use (gRPC metadata / HTTP header):
```
X-RW-Transport-Capabilities: prefetch=window:8;bundle=small;resume-token=true;dedupe-seq=true
```
ben: I like keeping it lightweight. main concern: prefetch window semantics need to be clearly defined. Is window the max number of items server may send without explicit ack? how does retry interact with that? short answer: define prefetch as "optimistic server push" and require resume-token for safe retry.
ben: if resume-token is present, client can dedupe on token boundaries; otherwise we must fall back to idempotent-only retries.
arun: For SDK ergonomics (py/ts/go) we should expose an explicit opt-in flag `enable_prefetch` and a `max_prefetch` param. Default off for python sync and go to avoid surprising memory spikes. TS async maybe default on for streaming UX.
jamie: Major risk: prefetch + retries => duplicates. If we rely on dedupe-seq then servers must include monotonically increasing seq per session. That's extra server work. alternative: require resume-token for safe resume and only allow prefetch when resume-token=true.
jamie: Also consider: prefetch-window should be advisory; servers can send fewer. Clients must not assume all items are final until they see terminal marker.
kate: On transport choices: gRPC metadata is easiest for internal Dedicated/Private. For hosted REST we'll need response headers or a negotiation endpoint (`/v1/transport-negotiation`). Keep payload tiny.
kate: We'll also need a fallback: if negotiation absent, SDKs pick `no-prefetch` and `resume-token=false` semantics.
ben: For retries: recommend two-level policy. Fast client retry (idempotent-only) when no resume-token. If resume-token present, allow longer-lived retry window with resume.
ben: Suggest we document these as default strategies per SDK and provide an escape hatch `transportHints` in client config.
mia: Agreed. Action items: 1) define header grammar; 2) wire a minimal negotiation in server for gRPC + REST; 3) update SDK surfaces with opt-in flags and clear defaults; 4) add tests for duplicate suppression and resume.
arun: Implementation notes: python sync should expose iterator API like `for item in client.list(..., prefetch=True, prefetch_size=8)` and keep memory bounded by queue size. TS should expose both `AsyncIterable` and an `autoPrefetch` option in constructor. Go should keep explicit buffered channel option.
jamie: On pagination: if server supports `server-cursor` we map iterator to `yield from cursor` semantics. If `prefetch-window` used, we implement background fetch with `max_inflight=window` and backpressure. Important: don't change public pagination tokens semantics — keep `page_token` stable.
kate: Edge cases: mixed capability across regions (some nodes support resume-token, some don't). We should route to nodes with strongest capability for routes that request prefetch; otherwise downgrade.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling out negotiation endpoint to staging now (deploy/3892) :rocket:
mia: Nice. Also let's add explicit telemetry hooks (capabilities seen, fallback events, duplicate_detected) so Optimize can recommend quantization/batching later.
ben: I'll draft the header grammar and small RFC follow-up. arun/jamie can prototype client glue. kate will sketch server endpoint mapping.
mia: Thanks all. I'll open the follow-up RFC and link PRs. :thumbsup:
